scientific_card_excerpt.text: Claim: For a Boolean f:{−1,1}^n→{−1,1}, let Δ_i(f)=H(f)−(H(f_i^+)+H(f_i^-))/2 and let I_i(f) be coordinate influence under the stated Fourier normalization. With h(t)=−t log_2 t−(1−t)log_2(1−t) and D(t)=h(t)+1−h(1/2+√(t(1−t))), the source proves 0≤Δ_i(f)≤D(I_i(f)) for every coordinate. For every even m≥2 it gives F_m and a distinguished z with p=2^-m, I_z(F_m)=p, Δ_z(F_m)=p log_2(1/p)+(3/ln 2)p−(19/(6 ln 2))p^2+O(p^3), and D(p)−Δ_z(F_m)=2p^2/ln 2+O(p^3), so Δ_z/I_z=m+3/ln 2+O(2^-m), while H(F_m)≤2I(F_m). Thus no universal bound Δ_i(f)≤C I_i(f) can hold for all Boolean functions and all prescribed coordinates.

source_excerpts.text:
The 8–10/10 foundational endpoint was not achieved in this session. The strongest complete result established is an asymptotically sharp theorem about Boolean Fourier entropy under restriction. It rules out a particular local proof strategy, but it does not resolve the Fourier Entropy–Influence conjecture, and its historical originality remains unestablished.
I investigated entropy couplings for union-closed families, covariance-based approaches to dimension-free concentration, and Gaussian-polynomial independence before and alongside the Fourier investigation. None yielded a complete foundational conclusion. The substantive result that survived is presented below, with its proof and exact limitations.
1. The foundational target
For a Boolean function \(f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}\), write
\[
\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E\!\left[f(X)\prod_{j\in S}X_j\right].
\]
Its squared Fourier coefficients form a probability distribution. Define its Fourier entropy and influences by
\[
H(f)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\widehat f(S)^2
       \log_2\frac1{\widehat f(S)^2},
\qquad
I_i(f)=\sum_{S\ni i}\widehat f(S)^2,
\qquad
I(f)=\sum_i I_i(f).
\]
Here \(I_i(f)\) is also the probability that flipping coordinate \(i\) changes the output.
The Fourier Entropy–Influence conjecture asks for a universal constant \(C\) such that
\[
H(f)\le C I(f)
\]
in every dimension. A restriction-based approach studies
\[
\Delta_i(f)
=
H(f)-\frac{H(f_i^+)+H(f_i^-)}2,
\]
where \(f_i^\pm\) fixes coordinate \(i\) to \(\pm1\). If every nonconstant Boolean function had a suitable coordinate satisfying \(\Delta_i(f)\le C I_i(f)\), induction would prove FEI. This approach is explicitly studied in the primary literature; it is not itself a new invention. arXiv
The calculation below establishes how badly the inequality can fail when the coordinate is prescribed rather than chosen.
2. The theorem actually established
Let
\[
h(t)=-t\log_2t-(1-t)\log_2(1-t)
\]
be binary entropy, and define
\[
D(t)
=
h(t)+1-h\!\left(\frac12+\sqrt{t(1-t)}\right).
\]
Local entropy modulus
For every Boolean function and every coordinate,
\[
\boxed{
0\le \Delta_i(f)\le D\!\left(I_i(f)\right).
}
\tag{1}
\]
Equality in the upper bound is possible only when
\[
I_i(f)\in\left\{0,\frac12,1\right\}.
\tag{2}
\]
The condition \(I_i(f)=1/2\) alone is not sufficient; the proof below gives the full equality criterion.
